## Setup
```{python}
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Find the digitalrodent folder
root = Path.cwd().parent

# Figures directory
fig_dir = root / "results" / "figures"
fig_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

# Load combined dataset
Combined_dataset = pd.read_csv(
    root / "results" / "combined_dataset" / "Combined_dataset.csv"
)

# Millimetres to inches for figure sizes
MM = 1 / 25.4

# Figure settings
plt.rcParams.update({
    "font.family": "Arial",
    "font.size": 6,
    "axes.labelsize": 8,
    "axes.titlesize": 8,
    "xtick.labelsize": 6,
    "ytick.labelsize": 6,
    "legend.fontsize": 6,
    "legend.title_fontsize": 6
})

print(Combined_dataset.shape)
```



```{python}

# --------------------------------------------------
# FIGURE 1: Acquisition protocol landscape
# One point = one unique acquisition protocol within a dataset
#
# x = TR
# y = TE
# bubble size = number of scans using that protocol
# fill colour = MRI field strength
# marker = fMRI sequence
# edge colour = awake / anesthetized
# --------------------------------------------------

df = Combined_dataset.copy()

# Numeric variables
df["MRI T.R."] = pd.to_numeric(
    df["MRI T.R."],
    errors="coerce"
)

df["MRI T.E."] = pd.to_numeric(
    df["MRI T.E."],
    errors="coerce"
)

# Extract MRI field strength
df["MRI_T"] = pd.to_numeric(
    df["MRI"]
    .astype(str)
    .str.extract(r"(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)")[0],
    errors="coerce"
)

# Clean categorical columns
for col in [
    "Coil",
    "fMRI.sequence",
    "Anesthesia",
    "Ventilation",
    "head-plate",
    "Habituation"
]:
    df[col] = (
        df[col]
        .astype(str)
        .str.strip()
        .replace(["nan", "NA", ""], np.nan)
    )

# --------------------------------------------------
# Awake / anesthetized grouping
# --------------------------------------------------

df["State"] = "Anesthetized"

awake_mask = (
    df["Anesthesia"]
    .fillna("")
    .str.lower()
    .str.contains("awake")
)

df.loc[awake_mask, "State"] = "Awake"

# Unknown if anesthesia itself is missing
df.loc[df["Anesthesia"].isna(), "State"] = "Unknown"

# --------------------------------------------------
# Create unique acquisition protocols
# --------------------------------------------------

protocol_columns = [
    "Dataset_name",
    "MRI_T",
    "Coil",
    "fMRI.sequence",
    "MRI T.R.",
    "MRI T.E.",
    "Anesthesia",
    "Anesthesia amount",
    "Ventilation",
    "head-plate",
    "Habituation",
    "State"
]

protocols = (
    df
    .groupby(
        protocol_columns,
        dropna=False
    )
    .agg(
        N_scans=("Scan_id", "count"),
        N_animals=("Participant_Id", "nunique")
    )
    .reset_index()
)

# Need TR and TE for the scatter
protocols = protocols.dropna(
    subset=["MRI T.R.", "MRI T.E."]
).copy()

# --------------------------------------------------
# Short dataset labels
# --------------------------------------------------

dataset_codes = {
    "Awake": "AW",
    "Awake_Rest": "AR",
    "Douglas": "DO",
    "Env_Enrichment": "EE",
    "Florida": "FL",
    "Longitudinal": "LO",
    "3xTG": "3T",
    "Multicenter": "MC",
    "Psilocybin": "PS",
    "Psilocybin_Pilot": "PP",
    "MPTP": "MP",
    "Sexdifference": "SD",
    "NDUFS4": "ND",
    "Propofol": "PR",
    "Alvino": "AL"
}

protocols["Label"] = (
    protocols["Dataset_name"]
    .map(dataset_codes)
    .fillna(protocols["Dataset_name"])
)

# --------------------------------------------------
# Marker per sequence
# --------------------------------------------------

sequence_levels = (
    protocols["fMRI.sequence"]
    .fillna("Unknown")
    .unique()
)

markers = [
    "o", "s", "^", "D", "v",
    "P", "X", "<", ">"
]

sequence_marker = {
    sequence: markers[i % len(markers)]
    for i, sequence in enumerate(sequence_levels)
}

# --------------------------------------------------
# Bubble size
# --------------------------------------------------

sizes = (
    45 +
    280 *
    protocols["N_scans"] /
    protocols["N_scans"].max()
)

# --------------------------------------------------
# Plot
# --------------------------------------------------

fig, ax = plt.subplots(
    figsize=(190 * MM, 130 * MM)
)

# State edge colours
state_edge = {
    "Awake": "steelblue",
    "Anesthetized": "sandybrown",
    "Unknown": "gray"
}

# Plot per sequence so markers differ
for sequence in sequence_levels:

    temp = protocols[
        protocols["fMRI.sequence"].fillna("Unknown") == sequence
    ]

    for idx, row in temp.iterrows():

        ax.scatter(
            row["MRI T.R."],
            row["MRI T.E."],
            s=sizes.loc[idx],
            c=[row["MRI_T"]],
            cmap="viridis",
            vmin=protocols["MRI_T"].min(),
            vmax=protocols["MRI_T"].max(),
            marker=sequence_marker[sequence],
            edgecolor=state_edge[row["State"]],
            linewidth=1.5,
            alpha=0.75,
            zorder=3
        )

        ax.annotate(
            row["Label"],
            (
                row["MRI T.R."],
                row["MRI T.E."]
            ),
            xytext=(4, 4),
            textcoords="offset points",
            fontsize=6,
            fontweight="bold"
        )

# --------------------------------------------------
# MRI colour bar
# --------------------------------------------------

sm = plt.cm.ScalarMappable(
    cmap="viridis",
    norm=plt.Normalize(
        protocols["MRI_T"].min(),
        protocols["MRI_T"].max()
    )
)

sm.set_array([])

cbar = plt.colorbar(
    sm,
    ax=ax,
    pad=0.02
)

cbar.set_label("MRI field strength (T)")

# --------------------------------------------------
# Sequence legend
# --------------------------------------------------

sequence_handles = []

for sequence in sequence_levels:

    sequence_handles.append(
        plt.Line2D(
            [0], [0],
            marker=sequence_marker[sequence],
            linestyle="",
            markerfacecolor="white",
            markeredgecolor="black",
            markersize=6,
            label=str(sequence)
        )
    )

legend1 = ax.legend(
    handles=sequence_handles,
    title="fMRI sequence",
    loc="upper left",
    frameon=False
)

ax.add_artist(legend1)

# --------------------------------------------------
# State legend
# --------------------------------------------------

state_handles = []

for state in [
    "Awake",
    "Anesthetized",
    "Unknown"
]:

    state_handles.append(
        plt.Line2D(
            [0], [0],
            marker="o",
            linestyle="",
            markerfacecolor="white",
            markeredgecolor=state_edge[state],
            markeredgewidth=1.5,
            markersize=6,
            label=state
        )
    )

ax.legend(
    handles=state_handles,
    title="State",
    loc="lower right",
    frameon=False
)

# --------------------------------------------------
# Styling
# --------------------------------------------------

ax.set_xlabel("Repetition time, TR")
ax.set_ylabel("Echo time, TE")
ax.set_title("Acquisition protocol landscape")

ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)

plt.tight_layout()

plt.savefig(
    fig_dir / "figure1_acquisition_protocols.svg",
    format="svg",
    bbox_inches="tight"
)

plt.show()

# Also print the protocol summary so you can inspect
# exactly what each plotted point represents
print(
    protocols[
        [
            "Dataset_name",
            "MRI_T",
            "Coil",
            "fMRI.sequence",
            "MRI T.R.",
            "MRI T.E.",
            "Anesthesia",
            "Anesthesia amount",
            "Ventilation",
            "head-plate",
            "Habituation",
            "N_scans"
        ]
    ]
)
```


```{python}
# --------------------------------------------------
# FIGURE 2: QC plot
# x = mean FD
# y = tSNR
# size = maximum FD
# colour = MRI field strength
# --------------------------------------------------

df = Combined_dataset.copy()

for col in ["FD average", "FD maximum", "tSNR"]:
    df[col] = pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors="coerce")

df["MRI_T"] = pd.to_numeric(
    df["MRI"].astype(str).str.extract(r"(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)")[0],
    errors="coerce"
)

plot_df = df.dropna(
    subset=["FD average", "FD maximum", "tSNR"]
).copy()

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(180 * MM, 130 * MM))

if len(plot_df) == 0:

    print("No scans currently have FD average + FD maximum + tSNR together.")

else:

    sizes = 20 + 220 * (
        plot_df["FD maximum"] /
        plot_df["FD maximum"].max()
    )

    sc = ax.scatter(
        plot_df["FD average"],
        plot_df["tSNR"],
        s=sizes,
        c=plot_df["MRI_T"],
        cmap="viridis",
        alpha=0.5,
        edgecolor="none"
    )

    cbar = plt.colorbar(sc, ax=ax)
    cbar.set_label("MRI field strength (T)")

    medians = (
        plot_df
        .groupby("Dataset_name")
        .agg(
            FD_mean=("FD average", "median"),
            tSNR=("tSNR", "median")
        )
    )

    ax.scatter(
        medians["FD_mean"],
        medians["tSNR"],
        s=55,
        color="sandybrown",
        edgecolor="black",
        linewidth=0.5,
        zorder=3
    )

    for dataset, row in medians.iterrows():
        ax.annotate(
            dataset,
            (row["FD_mean"], row["tSNR"]),
            xytext=(4, 4),
            textcoords="offset points",
            fontsize=5.8
        )

    ax.set_xlabel("Mean FD")
    ax.set_ylabel("tSNR")
    ax.set_title("Motion and signal quality")

    ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)

    plt.tight_layout()

    plt.savefig(
        fig_dir / "figure2_qc_tsnr.svg",
        format="svg",
        bbox_inches="tight"
    )

    plt.show()
```

```{python} --------------------------------------------------
# FIGURE 3: Dataset composition
# Bars = number of animals by sex
# Right side = aligned mini-table
# --------------------------------------------------

df = Combined_dataset.copy()
df["Age(week)"] = pd.to_numeric(df["Age(week)"], errors="coerce")

# One row per unique animal
animals = (
    df
    .dropna(subset=["Participant_Id"])
    .drop_duplicates(subset=["Dataset_name", "Participant_Id"])
    .copy()
)

animals["Sex_clean"] = (
    animals["Sex"]
    .astype(str)
    .str.upper()
    .str.strip()
)

# Number of scans
scan_counts = (
    df.groupby("Dataset_name")["Scan_id"]
    .count()
    .rename("N_scans")
)

# Number of animals
animal_counts = (
    animals.groupby("Dataset_name")["Participant_Id"]
    .nunique()
    .rename("N_animals")
)

# Mean age
mean_age = (
    animals.groupby("Dataset_name")["Age(week)"]
    .mean()
    .rename("Mean_age")
)

# Sex counts
sex_counts = (
    animals[animals["Sex_clean"].isin(["F", "M"])]
    .groupby(["Dataset_name", "Sex_clean"])
    .size()
    .unstack(fill_value=0)
)

if "F" not in sex_counts.columns:
    sex_counts["F"] = 0

if "M" not in sex_counts.columns:
    sex_counts["M"] = 0

# Strain
strain_summary = (
    animals.groupby("Dataset_name")["Rodent.strain"]
    .apply(
        lambda x: ", ".join(
            sorted(
                [
                    s
                    for s in x.dropna().astype(str).str.strip().unique()
                    if s.lower() not in ["", "na", "nan"]
                ]
            )
        )
    )
    .rename("Strain")
)

# Combine
summary = pd.concat(
    [
        scan_counts,
        animal_counts,
        mean_age,
        sex_counts[["F", "M"]],
        strain_summary
    ],
    axis=1
)

summary["F"] = summary["F"].fillna(0)
summary["M"] = summary["M"].fillna(0)

summary["Known_sex"] = summary["F"] + summary["M"]

summary["Unknown_sex"] = (
    summary["N_animals"] -
    summary["Known_sex"]
)

summary["Strain"] = summary["Strain"].fillna("NA")

summary.loc[
    summary["Strain"] == "",
    "Strain"
] = "NA"

# Smallest at top, largest at bottom
summary = summary.sort_values(
    "N_animals",
    ascending=True
)

y = np.arange(len(summary))

# --------------------------------------------------
# Figure
# --------------------------------------------------

fig, ax = plt.subplots(
    figsize=(210 * MM, 125 * MM)
)

# Female
ax.barh(
    y,
    summary["F"],
    color="sandybrown",
    label="Female"
)

# Male
ax.barh(
    y,
    summary["M"],
    left=summary["F"],
    color="steelblue",
    label="Male"
)

# Unknown sex
if (summary["Unknown_sex"] > 0).any():
    ax.barh(
        y,
        summary["Unknown_sex"],
        left=summary["F"] + summary["M"],
        color="lightgray",
        label="Sex unknown"
    )

# Dataset labels
ax.set_yticks(y)
ax.set_yticklabels(summary.index)

# --------------------------------------------------
# X axis stops at Multicenter
# --------------------------------------------------

if "Multicenter" in summary.index:
    x_max_plot = summary.loc[
        "Multicenter",
        "N_animals"
    ]
else:
    x_max_plot = summary["N_animals"].max()

ax.set_xlim(0, x_max_plot)

# --------------------------------------------------
# Mini-table
# Same y-coordinate as the bars
# --------------------------------------------------

# Positions relative to the right side of the graph
x_scans = x_max_plot * 1.04
x_age = x_max_plot * 1.25
x_strain = x_max_plot * 1.48

# Headers
ax.text(
    x_scans,
    -0.9,
    "Scans",
    fontweight="bold",
    fontsize=6,
    ha="left",
    clip_on=False
)

ax.text(
    x_age,
    -0.9,
    "Mean age",
    fontweight="bold",
    fontsize=6,
    ha="left",
    clip_on=False
)

ax.text(
    x_strain,
    -0.9,
    "Strain",
    fontweight="bold",
    fontsize=6,
    ha="left",
    clip_on=False
)

# Values
for yi, dataset in enumerate(summary.index):

    row = summary.loc[dataset]

    # Scan number
    ax.text(
        x_scans,
        yi,
        str(int(row["N_scans"])),
        va="center",
        ha="left",
        fontsize=6,
        clip_on=False
    )

    # Mean age
    if pd.isna(row["Mean_age"]):
        age_text = "NA"
    else:
        age_text = f'{row["Mean_age"]:.1f}'

    ax.text(
        x_age,
        yi,
        age_text,
        va="center",
        ha="left",
        fontsize=6,
        clip_on=False
    )

    # Strain
    ax.text(
        x_strain,
        yi,
        row["Strain"],
        va="center",
        ha="left",
        fontsize=5.5,
        clip_on=False
    )

# --------------------------------------------------
# Styling
# --------------------------------------------------

ax.set_xlabel("Number of animals")
ax.set_title("Dataset composition")
ax.invert_yaxis()

ax.legend(
    frameon=False,
    loc="upper right"
)

ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)

# Extra physical space on right for mini-table
plt.subplots_adjust(
    left=0.16,
    right=0.58,
    top=0.92,
    bottom=0.12
)

plt.savefig(
    fig_dir / "figure3_dataset_composition.svg",
    format="svg",
    bbox_inches="tight"
)

plt.show()
```



## Old code 
This code generates a heatmap to visualize the mean component values for each dataset. To see which datasets may have generally higher or lower values.
```{python}
from matplotlib.colors import LinearSegmentedColormap

components = [f"comp{i}" for i in range(1, 19)]

Combined_dataset[components] = Combined_dataset[components].apply(
    pd.to_numeric,
    errors="coerce"
)


# ============================================================
# 1. RAW COMPONENT HEATMAP
# ============================================================

heatmap_data = (
    Combined_dataset
    .groupby("Dataset_name")[components]
    .median()
)

cmap = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list(
    "steelblue_sandybrown",
    ["steelblue", "lightblue", "wheat", "sandybrown"]
)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(180 * MM, 100 * MM))

im = ax.imshow(
    heatmap_data.values,
    aspect="auto",
    cmap=cmap
)

ax.set_xticks(range(len(components)))
ax.set_xticklabels(
    components,
    rotation=45,
    ha="right"
)

ax.set_yticks(range(len(heatmap_data.index)))
ax.set_yticklabels(heatmap_data.index)

ax.set_xlabel("Component")
ax.set_ylabel("Dataset")
ax.set_title("Median component value per dataset")

cbar = plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax)
cbar.set_label("Median value")

plt.tight_layout()

plt.savefig(
    fig_dir / "component_heatmap.svg",
    format="svg",
    bbox_inches="tight"
)

plt.show()


# ============================================================
# 2. STANDARDIZED COMPONENT HEATMAP
# ============================================================

heatmap_z = heatmap_data.sub(
    heatmap_data.mean(axis=1),
    axis=0
)

heatmap_z = heatmap_z.div(
    heatmap_data.std(axis=1).replace(0, np.nan),
    axis=0
)

limit = np.nanmax(np.abs(heatmap_z.values))

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(180 * MM, 100 * MM))

im = ax.imshow(
    heatmap_z.values,
    aspect="auto",
    cmap=cmap,
    vmin=-limit,
    vmax=limit
)

ax.set_xticks(range(len(components)))
ax.set_xticklabels(
    components,
    rotation=45,
    ha="right"
)

ax.set_yticks(range(len(heatmap_z.index)))
ax.set_yticklabels(heatmap_z.index)

ax.set_xlabel("Component")
ax.set_ylabel("Dataset")
ax.set_title("Relative component pattern per dataset")

cbar = plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax)
cbar.set_label("Z-score")

plt.tight_layout()

plt.savefig(
    fig_dir / "component_heatmap_zscore.svg",
    format="svg",
    bbox_inches="tight"
)

plt.show()
```

Ridgeline plots for each component across datasets.
```{python}
from scipy.stats import gaussian_kde

components = [f"comp{i}" for i in range(1, 19)]

# Possibility to isolate/remove a specific dataset
plot_data = Combined_dataset
# plot_data = Combined_dataset[Combined_dataset["Dataset_name"] != "Alvino"]

# Make sure component columns are numeric
plot_data[components] = plot_data[components].apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce")

cutoff = 1.5

# Order datasets by overall mean across all components
dataset_order = (
    plot_data
    .groupby("Dataset_name")[components]
    .mean()
    .mean(axis=1)
    .sort_values(ascending=False)
    .index
)

# Shared x-range, but plot only up to cutoff
x_min = plot_data[components].min().min()
x = np.linspace(x_min, cutoff, 300)

# 18 distinct colors
colors = plt.cm.tab20(np.linspace(0, 1, len(components)))

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(180 * MM, 120 * MM))

above_cutoff = []

for i, dataset in enumerate(dataset_order):

    ax.hlines(
        y=i,
        xmin=x_min,
        xmax=cutoff,
        color="lightgray",
        linewidth=0.6,
        zorder=1
    )

    for j, component in enumerate(components):

        values = (
            plot_data.loc[
                plot_data["Dataset_name"] == dataset,
                component
            ]
            .dropna()
            .astype(float)
        )

        if len(values) < 2:
            continue

        kde = gaussian_kde(values)
        density = kde(x)

        if density.max() == 0:
            continue

        density = density / density.max() * 0.75

        ax.plot(
            x,
            i + density,
            color=colors[j],
            alpha=0.7,
            linewidth=0.9,
            label=component if i == 0 else None,
            zorder=2
        )

        ax.fill_between(
            x,
            i,
            i + density,
            color=colors[j],
            alpha=0.08,
            zorder=2
        )

        n_above = (values > cutoff).sum()

        if n_above > 0:
            above_cutoff.append([
                dataset,
                component,
                n_above,
                values.max()
            ])

            ax.scatter(
                [cutoff],
                [i + 0.72],
                color="red",
                s=8,
                zorder=4
            )

ax.set_yticks(range(len(dataset_order)))
ax.set_yticklabels(dataset_order)

ax.set_xlim(x_min, cutoff)
ax.set_xlabel("DR value")
ax.set_ylabel("Dataset")
ax.set_title("Overlapping DR distributions of all 18 components per dataset")

ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)

ax.legend(
    title="Component",
    frameon=False,
    ncol=3,
    bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1),
    loc="upper left"
)

plt.tight_layout()

plt.savefig(
    fig_dir / "ridgeline_all_components_overlapping_cutoff_1_5.svg",
    format="svg",
    bbox_inches="tight"
)

plt.show()


# ============================================================
# TABLE OF VALUES ABOVE CUTOFF
# ============================================================

above_cutoff_df = pd.DataFrame(
    above_cutoff,
    columns=["Dataset_name", "Component", "N_above_1.5", "Max_value"]
)

if len(above_cutoff_df) == 0:
    print("No values above 1.5 were found.")
else:
    above_cutoff_df = above_cutoff_df.sort_values(
        ["N_above_1.5", "Max_value"],
        ascending=[False, False]
    )
    print(above_cutoff_df.to_string(index=False))
```


Following code does everything that has already been done for the datasets for the normative model for the Alzheimer dataset.
## Alzheimer 
```{python}
from scipy.stats import gaussian_kde

Alzheimer = pd.read_csv(
    root / "data" / "Alzheimer" / "Alzheimer_MetaData.tsv",
    sep="\t"
)

components = [f"comp{i}" for i in range(1, 19)]

TG = Combined_dataset[
    Combined_dataset["Dataset_name"] == "3xTG"
]

Alzheimer[components] = Alzheimer[components].apply(
    pd.to_numeric,
    errors="coerce"
)

TG[components] = TG[components].apply(
    pd.to_numeric,
    errors="coerce"
)

# Shared x-range based on the actual data
all_values = pd.concat(
    [
        Alzheimer[components].stack(),
        TG[components].stack()
    ]
)

x_min = all_values.min()
x_max = all_values.max()

x = np.linspace(x_min, x_max, 300)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(180 * MM, 120 * MM))

for i, component in enumerate(components):

    # Alzheimer
    values_alzheimer = (
        Alzheimer[component]
        .dropna()
        .astype(float)
    )

    if len(values_alzheimer) >= 2:

        kde = gaussian_kde(values_alzheimer)
        density = kde(x)

        if density.max() > 0:

            density = density / density.max() * 0.75

            ax.fill_between(
                x,
                i,
                i + density,
                color="steelblue",
                alpha=0.25
            )

            ax.plot(
                x,
                i + density,
                color="steelblue",
                linewidth=1.2,
                label="Alzheimer" if i == 0 else None
            )


    # 3xTG
    values_tg = (
        TG[component]
        .dropna()
        .astype(float)
    )

    if len(values_tg) >= 2:

        kde = gaussian_kde(values_tg)
        density = kde(x)

        if density.max() > 0:

            density = density / density.max() * 0.75

            ax.fill_between(
                x,
                i,
                i + density,
                color="sandybrown",
                alpha=0.25
            )

            ax.plot(
                x,
                i + density,
                color="sandybrown",
                linewidth=1.2,
                label="3xTG" if i == 0 else None
            )


    ax.hlines(
        y=i,
        xmin=x_min,
        xmax=x_max,
        color="lightgray",
        linewidth=0.6,
        zorder=0
    )

ax.set_yticks(range(len(components)))
ax.set_yticklabels(components)

ax.set_xlim(x_min, x_max)

ax.set_xlabel("DR value")
ax.set_ylabel("Component")
ax.set_title("Alzheimer and 3xTG component distributions")

ax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
ax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)

ax.legend(
    frameon=False,
    loc="upper right"
)

plt.tight_layout()

plt.savefig(
    fig_dir / "Alzheimer_3xTG_ridgeline_components.svg",
    format="svg",
    bbox_inches="tight"
)

plt.show()
```


## statistical test 

```{python}
from scipy.stats import mannwhitneyu
from statsmodels.stats.multitest import multipletests

results = []

for component in components:

    alz = Alzheimer[component].dropna().astype(float)
    tg = TG[component].dropna().astype(float)

    stat, p = mannwhitneyu(
        alz,
        tg,
        alternative="two-sided"
    )

    results.append([
        component,
        len(alz),
        len(tg),
        alz.median(),
        tg.median(),
        stat,
        p
    ])

results = pd.DataFrame(
    results,
    columns=[
        "Component",
        "N_Alzheimer",
        "N_3xTG",
        "Median_Alzheimer",
        "Median_3xTG",
        "U",
        "p"
    ]
)

results["p_FDR"] = multipletests(
    results["p"],
    method="fdr_bh"
)[1]

print(
    results.sort_values("p_FDR").to_string(index=False)
)

```
